findings.summary: L125's mechanism (a subnormal operand's exponent field setting the wgmma window) may also break DotF16; num-dot's fp16 Part 2 has the same input gap L125 names for fp8
findings.detail: L125 withdrew the fp8 whole-dot facts. On wgmma a chunk is aligned to the largest exponent field, a subnormal operand's field reads as the smallest normal's, and so a product with a subnormal operand can set the window while its magnitude is far below it. evidence/num-dot's Part 2 'had no input where a product with a subnormal operand sets the window'. Its fp16 rows (DotF16, both paths) come from the same Part 2 input kinds, and I see no check of this case for 16-bit operands: num-dot-chunk tests fp8 only, and its mma.sync part checks against the loose fp8 chunk bound. If fp16 wgmma aligns the same way, take a = 2^-24 (a subnormal float16, field -14) times b = 2^15: the product is 2^-9 but its field is 2^1, so the unit is about 2^-22. Fifteen more products just below 2^-22 in the same chunk of 16 would be lost, about 3.6e-6. DotF16 allows 18*2^-22*(|acc| + sum|a*b|), about 8.4e-9 here, plus 18*2^-126: roughly 400 times less. Whether the device does this is a library question I cannot check, and I do not claim it does. matmul_f16 cites DotF16, and its inputs may hold subnormal float16 values (Pre allows any; randn cast to float16 contains some at the benchmark's sizes). Suggest the library run num-dot's fp16 and bf16 checks with a subnormal-operand product setting the window, or count subnormal operands as DotF8Chunk's liftMag does. Non-blocking: I re-accept the items.
findings.evidence: docs/library-review/ISSUES.md L125; docs/rules/num.md, the tl.dot chunk model and device questions (alignment bullet); evidence/num-dot Part 2 input kinds and its round-24 note
